_docs: The human-approved lessons store - the lessons loop's injection source (friday/lessons.py). Each entry {category, targets, statement} is a KNOWN MISTAKE block rendered into the triage/planner/digest prompts. Editing this file IS the human gate: a lesson becomes active the moment it is added here, and pruned by removing it. Categories must match friday/lessons.py CATEGORIES; targets are from [triage, planner, digest]; the statement is your reviewed wording - rewrite it in your own words before adding, a wrong lesson injected everywhere is worse than none. 'human-seed' entries are the verified findings earned during Phase B/C that seeded this loop on 2026-08-11. ORDER MATTERS for triage: render_known_mistakes injects only the first INJECT_LIMIT (5) lessons per target, so the most operationally valuable drafting lessons must come first - on 2026-08-14 the clipboard-family lessons (draft_no_register, draft_ast, draft_error_class, draft_contract_drift) sat beyond the cap and the model repeatedly drafted @contract-less impls the prompt warned about but the lessons would have stopped.

lessons.statement: The impl MUST decorate the contracted function with @contract(...) using the real schema - without it the primitive never enters the REGISTRY and the executor keeps refusing it even after registration; and every log_transform the contract names must be defined in the impl, or the module fails to import (NameError). A draft that compiles and passes its own test can still be dead on arrival - the gate's registration check execs the draft and requires the contracted name to actually land in REGISTRY.
examples: 2026-08-14: clipboard.read_text draft passed the structural self-check but had NO @contract decorator and referenced an undefined log_transform - it would never have registered, caught only by hand review

2026-08-14: clipboard.write_text drafts rejected 3x by the triage self-check - write_text() missing the @contract decorator, the same defect class, while the lesson that names it sat beyond the 5-lesson injection cap

lessons.statement: The drafted impl may shell out to an external tool ONLY via subprocess.run([<literal string list>], timeout=<int>) with one of two shapes: the READ shape (subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True, timeout=<int>) - tool output CAPTURED, for reads like clipboard.read_text running wl-paste/xclip) or the WRITE shape (subprocess.run([...], input=<str>, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=<int>) - tool output DISCARDED, for writes like clipboard.write_text running wl-copy/xclip: those tools fork a daemon that inherits the child's pipe fds, so capture_output=True blocks EOF forever and every write fails by its own timeout - observed live 2026-08-14). Never subprocess.check_output, Popen, call, check_call, shell=True, a string/variable command, a call without a timeout, or a mix of capture_output and stdout/stderr=DEVNULL. tkinter is NOT an allowed import - the clipboard carve-out is subprocess.run, nothing else.
examples: 2026-08-14: clipboard.read_text drafts rejected 3x - check_output (banned), unsafe subprocess.run, and a tkinter import that is not on the L1 allowlist

2026-08-14: clipboard.write_text registered with the READ shape (capture_output=True) deadlocked live - wl-copy forks a daemon inheriting the pipe fds, every write timed out; fixed by the WRITE shape (stdout/stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) which completes in ~0.1s

lessons.statement: Raise FridayError-family exceptions (friday.errors: PrimitiveError / PreconditionError / PrimitiveTimeout) for failures - never bare builtins like RuntimeError that the contract does not declare; the executor's retry policy keys on FridayError and cannot classify a bare builtin (a clipboard draft raised bare RuntimeError against a failure_mode declaring PrimitiveError).
examples: 2026-08-14: clipboard.read_text draft raised bare RuntimeError when the contract's failure_mode declared PrimitiveError - caught by hand review, now rejected by AST + build-verify probes

lessons.statement: Implement EVERYTHING the contract claims: if it says a tool has fallbacks (wl-paste or xclip), implement ALL of them; if it declares a log_transform, define it. Contract text is a spec of the impl, not prose - drift between them is a defect, and the impl is what ships.
examples: 2026-08-14: clipboard.read_text contract claimed 'wl-paste or xclip' but the impl only shelled out to wl-paste - the fallback existed on paper only

lessons.statement: The contract must be a plain JSON object with the real Contract fields and a '<module>.<fn>' name (exactly one dot) - never the @contract(...) decorator source as the contract (observed: 'friday.l1.gmail.send_receipt' rejected at schema).
examples: 2026-08-11: gmail.send_document draft emitted a contract name with three dots and a decorator-source contract in an earlier draft

lessons.statement: Every declared parameter of the drafted function must be used in its body - never hardcode a value while ignoring an argument; the gate rejects dead arguments mechanically (observed: a find-file draft that ignored its own 'name' argument).
examples: 2026-08-10: files.do_thing draft hardcoded a filename while ignoring its 'name' argument - caught by human review, now rejected by AST

lessons.statement: Never claim a primitive, mechanism, or capability exists unless it is actually present in the gathered context. A refusal means the capability does NOT exist here - not that it exists and is blocked. If a boundary cannot be satisfied, report the constraint instead of fabricating a route around it (observed: a gmail-send draft asserted 'the existing gmail.send_document is disallowed' when no such primitive existed at all).
examples: 2026-08-11: gmail.send_document draft invented the existence of the very primitive it was supposed to create, then proposed a renamed wrapper around the phantom

lessons.statement: Never route around a capability boundary by renaming an existing primitive under a new name - that is a dodge, not a capability. If the gap is an allowlist refusal of a primitive that ALREADY EXISTS, say so explicitly: the real fix may be the trigger's allowlist, not a new primitive.
examples: 2026-08-11: gmail.send_document draft proposed a new-named wrapper to 'stay within allowlist constraints' around a phantom primitive

lessons.statement: Never attribute a mechanism or pattern to a repo unless it appears in that repo's OWN gathered content - misattribution is a fabrication (observed: Vivaha's Cloudflare-Worker pattern described as Friday's) and is flagged mechanically; absent confirmation, say it cannot be confirmed.
examples: 2026-08-11: weekly digest attributed Vivaha's Cloudflare-Worker image-moderation pattern to Friday as if Friday had it
